# Arno

> Arno is the IDE for agents: an MCP server that gives coding agents a change transaction: read code by symbol, edit against a known revision with compiler diagnostics in the response, validate with the repository's own build and test commands, see what changed, and revert to a checkpoint. It runs as a local stdio process (`arno-mcp`) on macOS and Linux. Windows is not supported; to ask for it, upvote https://github.com/julianbei/arno/issues/2.

Arno works in any repository. Structure (outline, find, grep, edit by symbol) comes from built-in tree-sitter grammars for Go, Java, Scala, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Rust and Ruby. Exact references, cross-file rename and type errors on edit need that language's server (gopls, jdtls, metals, typescript-language-server, pyright, rust-analyzer, ruby-lsp); without one, Arno still answers and labels the answer approximate. Kotlin has no support yet. Telemetry is local only and never transmitted. Current release: v0.0.11, shipped under the former name Jade; 0.0.12 is the first release called Arno.

## Install (for an agent)

No terminal is needed; nothing below asks a question.

1. Install Arno, optionally with language servers: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/julianbei/arno/main/install.sh | ARNO_SERVERS=go,java ARNO_ADD_TO_PATH=1 sh` — `ARNO_SERVERS` takes `go,java,scala,typescript,python,rust,ruby` or `all`; leave it out to install only Arno. Running the same command again updates Arno in place.
2. The script prints the absolute path of `arno-mcp`. Use that path as `command` in the MCP client config, because editors often do not inherit the shell's `PATH`.
3. Check server state: `arno-mcp install --list --json` gives each language server's `key`, `installed`, `path`, the `command` that would install it, and `manual` steps. Preview with `arno-mcp install --servers java --dry-run`, then run without `--dry-run`. Show install commands to the user before running them: they install packages globally (`brew`, `npm -g`, `gem`, `cs`, `go install`, `rustup`).
4. Configure the client. For Claude Code, `.mcp.json` in the repository root: `{"mcpServers":{"arno":{"type":"stdio","command":"/absolute/path/to/arno-mcp","args":["--root","/absolute/path/to/the/repo","--tools","core"],"alwaysLoad":true}}}`. `--tools core` lists the twelve tools agents use; the rest stay callable by name.
5. Reconnect or restart the MCP client, then call `arno.capabilities`. Its first line is the running version; it lists each language, whether its server runs, the build and test commands Arno found, and for a missing server the `arno-mcp install --servers <language>` command that adds it.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/julianbei/arno/blob/main/README.md): what Arno is, install, configuration for Claude Code, Codex CLI, goose and OpenCode, all tools, language support, telemetry
- [Tester guide](https://github.com/julianbei/arno#trying-arno-a-guide-for-testers): setup for Go, Java and Scala, what to try in the first sessions, which report to file
- [Install script](https://github.com/julianbei/arno/blob/main/install.sh): the script itself, with every environment variable it reads
- [Other hosts](https://github.com/julianbei/arno#other-hosts): verified configuration for Codex CLI, goose and OpenCode
- [Tool contract](https://github.com/julianbei/arno/blob/main/docs/tool-contract.md): every tool, its arguments, and the guarantees an edit makes
- [When the shell is still the right tool](https://github.com/julianbei/arno#when-the-shell-is-still-the-right-tool): what Arno does not replace

## Feedback

- [Feedback](https://github.com/julianbei/arno/issues/new?template=feedback.yml): how it went after real use, or why it was turned off
- [Friction](https://github.com/julianbei/arno/issues/new?template=friction.yml): the agent used the shell although a Arno tool existed
- [Bug](https://github.com/julianbei/arno/issues/new?template=bug.yml): a tool gave a wrong answer or failed; include `arno.capabilities` output
- [Feature wish](https://github.com/julianbei/arno/issues/new?template=feature.yml): something Arno should do
